changes.summary: Native startup shares caller cancellation through launch admission and bootstrap transport. A late or abandoned child is aborted and joined; the original helper API remains available.
Failed or canceled startup retires both unbound native owners concurrently, joins both receipts and retains every cleanup error. Successful lease recovery ordering is unchanged.

regressions.result: PASS; canceled caller starts no child.
PASS; 20ms late launch under a 10ms deadline receives no bootstrap and is killed once and joined.
PASS; blocked bootstrap uses the 10ms caller deadline instead of a fresh 2s IPC budget.
PASS; 2ms launch plus concurrent 10ms/20ms retirement takes 22ms instead of the prior serial 32ms. Both owners join; cancellation, cleanup failure and uncertain recovery remain distinguishable.

initialFailures: An initial compilation failure from the changed startup helper signature was corrected by retaining the original wrapper; residentagent tests subsequently passed.

An initial inputworker run timed out in the existing 50ms TestSourceWriterSlowAuthorizationYieldsToHeartbeat/command-ack assertion. The focused rerun and final full inputworker run passed with that test unchanged; the transient failure's cause was not established.

limitations: Fixture durations use synctest virtual time, not measured product performance.
These changes reduce canceled/failed startup work and serial cleanup delay. They do not remove the normal successful entry's observed 166.629ms grant median or 123.648ms native pair startup median.
Native process creation cannot itself be interrupted by this helper; a launch completing after cancellation is instead retired before returning.
Cleanup retains its existing bounded Close and ExitPending rules; the caller deadline is not proof that native cleanup finished.
A source/query/gate disconnect root cause, capture/apply tails, hosted CI COM failures and installer cleanup failures remain independent unresolved paths.
